statement: A straight segment joins the points (2, 3) and (14, 21). How many points with both coordinates whole numbers lie on this segment, including its two ends?

choices.misconception: I found the 6 equal steps between the whole-number points and counted the steps instead of the points.
I found the right points but left out both ends of the segment.
I thought there is a whole-number point above every whole number x from 2 to 14, which gave 13.
I thought there is a whole-number point beside every whole number y from 3 to 21, which gave 19.

hints: How far does the segment go across, and how far up?
From one end to the other is 12 across and 18 up. The whole-number points split it into equal steps, each a whole number across and a whole number up. Use the greatest common divisor.
The greatest common divisor of 12 and 18 is 6, so each step is 2 across and 3 up.

solutions.reliable: From (2, 3) to (14, 21) the segment goes 12 across and 18 up, so every 2 across it goes 3 up. A whole-number point on the segment must be a whole number of these 2-across, 3-up steps from (2, 3), because 2 and 3 have no common factor. That gives (2, 3), (4, 6), (6, 9), (8, 12), (10, 15), (12, 18), (14, 21): 6 steps and 7 points. The transferable idea: a segment between lattice points going a across and b up contains $\gcd(a, b) + 1$ lattice points.

whyOnTest: Tests lattice reasoning: whole-number points on a segment come in equal steps set by the greatest common divisor of the run and the rise.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
